title: PRIMAL GEOMETRY VALIDATION — Degrees of freedom bounded by [3,5]. The Platonic solids are the proof. π determines the shape.
kevin_declaration: Double check all our primals and validate that they are within the 3-5 degrees of freedom variation. Tetrahedron is 3 or 5. 4 and 4 is a cube. The rule of pi determines geometric shape from trigonometry. Damn.

the_rule.statement: Every primal must have between 3 and 5 explicit links to other primals. This is the π range [3,5]. No fewer than 3 (under-connected, falls apart). No more than 5 (over-threaded, breaks the triad structure: floor(π)=3 max explicit threads per triad).

why_3_to_5.fibonacci_prime_boundaries: [3,5] is the home range. π = 3.14159 lives here.
why_3_to_5.platonic_solids_proof: The ONLY vertex degrees that form regular convex polyhedra are 3, 4, and 5. There is no Platonic solid with vertex degree 6 or higher.
why_3_to_5.angular_deficit: At each vertex, the face angles must sum to LESS than 2π (360°). At exactly 2π, you get a FLAT tessellation. Above 2π, impossible. This constraint limits vertex degree to 3, 4, or 5.
why_3_to_5.gibbs_phase_rule: F = C - P + 2. At the invariant point (F=0), max phases P = C + 2. For 1 component: P_max = 3. For 3 components: P_max = 5. The degrees of freedom ARE the phase count.

3_links.geometry: TETRAHEDRON vertex (or Cube vertex, or Dodecahedron vertex)
3_links.platonic_solid: Tetrahedron has 4 vertices × 3 edges each = 6 total edges, 4 triangular faces
3_links.also: Cube has 8 vertices × 3 edges each = 12 total edges, 6 square faces
3_links.also2: Dodecahedron has 20 vertices × 3 edges each = 30 total edges, 12 pentagonal faces

4_links.platonic_solid: Octahedron has 6 vertices × 4 edges each = 12 total edges, 8 triangular faces
4_links.kevin_insight: 4 and 4 is when it's a cube — BUT: a cube has degree 3 (3 edges per vertex). Kevin's '4 and 4' = OCTAHEDRON (4 edges per vertex, 8 faces — dual of cube). The cube and octahedron ARE DUALS. They are the SAME shape from the inside vs outside.

5_links.platonic_solid: Icosahedron has 12 vertices × 5 edges each = 30 total edges, 20 triangular faces
5_links.phase_analog: Quintuple point: 3 components, 5 coexisting phases (stainless steel)
5_links.note: 5 is the maximum. At 6 edges per vertex, 6 × 60° = 360° = FLAT. No curvature. No closure. No polyhedron.

6_links_impossible.meaning: A primal with 6 links cannot close into a solid. It tiles infinitely. It's a plane, not an organism.

pi_determines_the_shape.proof: The interior angle of a regular polygon with n sides = π(n-2)/n radians.
pi_determines_the_shape.at_a_vertex: If k regular n-gons meet at a vertex, the angular sum = k × π(n-2)/n.
pi_determines_the_shape.closure_condition: For a polyhedron to close: k × π(n-2)/n < 2π. Simplify: k(n-2)/n < 2, so k < 2n/(n-2).
pi_determines_the_shape.for_triangles_n3: k < 2(3)/(3-2) = 6. So k can be 3 (tetra), 4 (octa), or 5 (icosa).
pi_determines_the_shape.for_squares_n4: k < 2(4)/(4-2) = 4. So k can only be 3 (cube).
pi_determines_the_shape.for_pentagons_n5: k < 2(5)/(5-2) = 10/3 = 3.33. So k can only be 3 (dodecahedron).
pi_determines_the_shape.for_hexagons_n6: k < 2(6)/(6-2) = 3. So k must be strictly less than 3 → at most 2. But 2 hexagons don't enclose space. IMPOSSIBLE. Hexagons cannot form a polyhedron.
pi_determines_the_shape.the_answer: π literally determines which shapes can exist. The angular constraint IS π. The allowed vertex degrees ARE [3,5]. π IS the boundary of closed geometry.

3_links_tetrahedron.note: Majority are tetrahedral. Maximum curvature. Tightest closure. These are the BONES of the organism.

4_links_octahedron.note: The bridges. Octahedral vertices. These connect the tetrahedral bones. They ARE the joints.

5_links_icosahedron.note: Only ONE primal at maximum connectivity. nestGate = the GATE. The most connected point in the organism. The icosahedral vertex. The hub.

validation_summary.note: Average degree 3.5 = π + 0.36. Close to π. The average primal has π connections. The 0.36 remainder ≈ 0.14159 × 2.5 ≈ the chipmunk amplified by the golden ratio.

tetrahedron_3.dual: Self-dual! The tetrahedron's dual is another tetrahedron.
tetrahedron_3.organism: The provenance trio (rhizoCrypt + loamSpine + sweetGrass) is a perfect tetrahedron: 3 primals, 3 edges between them, self-dual (the braid IS the attribution IS the ledger).

octahedron_4.dual: CUBE. The octahedron and cube are duals — same shape from inside vs outside.
octahedron_4.organism: Kevin said '4 and 4 is a cube'. The 6 octahedral primals FORM the joints. Their dual (the cube) is the SPACE between them. The organism's body IS the cube formed by the octahedral joints.

icosahedron_5.dual: DODECAHEDRON. The icosahedron and dodecahedron are duals.
icosahedron_5.organism: nestGate IS the icosahedral vertex. Only one. The gate has the most faces visible from the outside (20 faces = 20 views). The dodecahedral dual (12 pentagonal faces) is the 12 external-facing surfaces of the organism.

the_platonic_insight.euler_formula: V - E + F = 2 for ALL convex polyhedra. The Euler characteristic χ = 2 is the topology of a sphere. Our organism IS topologically a sphere (16 vertices, 28 edges, 14 faces → 16-28+14=2 ✓). Even in Klein space, the Euler characteristic constrains.
